clue.text: Completely honest followers of Scarborough and Leicester

parts.note: the folk song is Scarborough Fair, so the word that follows Scarborough there is a fair
taken as written
Leicester Square is a famous square in London's West End, so the word following Leicester is square

explanation.surface: Someone praises the decent folk of two English towns, Scarborough and Leicester.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarborough Fair is a traditional English ballad; Leicester Square is a London plaza of cinemas. The word that follows each place name, joined by AND, makes the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for dealing justly and without any cheating, so wholly honest.

clue.text: A really quiet rest can bring calm

parts.note: pianissimo, written pp in music, means very quiet
ease is rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: A spell of hush and repose can bring tranquillity.
explanation.definitionFit: To calm someone, especially an angry person, is to placate or pacify them with concessions.

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words three lanes

explanation.surface: A swimmer is told to do lengths across three lanes of the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swim' looks like an instruction to the swimmer, but it is the head swimming: feeling giddy.
explanation.definitionFit: When your head swims you feel dizzy and stagger, which is the verb sense of the word here.

parts.note: a bird making its home in a tree is building a little tree-house, so the phrase describes a bird at work

explanation.surface: Someone is constructing a child's den up in the branches.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds that construct a home of twigs among branches are making nests, a playful tree-house.

clue.text: A contest between two Poles and old Arab

indicators.note: between means the other pieces go inside the pair of poles

parts.note: the two poles of the earth are South and North, S and N
a race is a contest of speed

explanation.surface: A competition is staged between two Polish people and an elderly Arab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like Polish people; it is the geographic poles, S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval Christian writers used this name for the Muslim Arabs of the Crusades era.

parts.note: it reads like ironing clothes, but pressing someone means pushing them hard to do something

explanation.surface: An instruction to get on with the ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: To press or exhort somebody earnestly is to spur them on, the verb meant here.

clue.text: Meetings of supporters possibly raise about £50

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the money
possibly says the letters of raise may be put in another order

parts.note: L stands for a pound (libra) and L is also the Roman numeral 50, so £50 gives two Ls

explanation.surface: Gatherings of fans might bring in around fifty pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles the fodder to RAIES, and 'about' wraps it round the money: the pound sign is L (Latin libra) and fifty is L in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Political or sporting gatherings where backers assemble en masse to show support.

clue.text: Revamped edited files as classical carol for the faithful

indicators.note: revamped means overhauled, so these letters are made over into a new order

explanation.surface: Computer files that have been edited are revamped into a classic Christmas carol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the fodder. The Latin title translates as O Come, All Ye Faithful; this grid spells it FIDELIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin hymn sung at Christmas, a classical carol whose first words address the faithful.

clue.text: Not a chorister is out of tune in such an arrangement

indicators.note: out of tune suggests the notes are wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A choir member singing flat ruins the musical arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link word; the fodder is NOT A CHORISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring music for the instruments of a band is a musical arrangement.

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for editor is read backwards

parts.note: the press is journalism and newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: An editor going back to newspaper work feels disheartened.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten or deject someone is to discourage them, lowering their spirits.

definitions.meaning: uniform as an adjective means even, constant, steady
one who wears a uniform is a soldier, and a professional standing-army soldier is called this

explanation.definitionFit: Even or consistent is uniform; a full-time soldier in the standing army also bears this name.

definitions.meaning: to remain is to stop where you are, not leave
a prop or brace, such as a rope steadying a mast

explanation.definitionFit: To stop on is to remain; a supporting rope or corset bone is also so called.

clue.text: Left out of clique, charming hostess whose guests made pigs of themselves

definitions.text: charming hostess whose guests made pigs of themselves

indicators.note: out of means the letter for left is removed from the group

parts.note: a circle is a clique or set of friends

explanation.surface: Someone is excluded from a social set by a hostess whose diners overate.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Odyssey the enchantress turns Odysseus's crew into swine; 'charming' means casting charms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek sorceress of Homer's epic who entertained sailors and literally transformed them into swine.

clue.text: Abundant Religious Instruction given by church

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Religious Instruction, a school subject

explanation.surface: Plenty of Bible lessons are provided by the local parish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentiful or copious, as in a land full of resources or wildlife.

parts.note: it reads like a timetable entry, but the moment a baby arrives in the world is meant

explanation.surface: A query about when a train or flight is due.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn arriving in the world; the time of delivery is when life begins.

clue.text: Fossil resin that should be approached with caution

definitions.meaning: a hardened yellow tree gum from prehistoric times

definitions.text: that should be approached with caution
definitions.meaning: the traffic light between green and red tells drivers to take care

explanation.definitionFit: Fossilised tree gum, and also the yellow traffic signal warning drivers to slow down.

parts.note: it reads like the hour of revenge, but making scores level is levelling them, and late day is also a time

explanation.surface: A moment to take revenge on old enemies.
explanation.definitionFit: The close of the day is a time, and levelling the scores makes them equal.

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them afresh, so seems in is rearranged

explanation.surface: Vengeance looks fitting and proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' reads as one phrase, but 'in' belongs to the fodder and 'order' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of vengeance gave her name to any deserved downfall or punishment.

indicators.note: sloppy work is careless and messy, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone was sacked for careless copy-editing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' looks like being dismissed; it means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Set alight or kindled, as a fire or engine might be when started.

indicators.note: resorts read as re-sorts, sorting the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about sunny holiday destinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorts' looks like a noun for holiday spots; read it as re-sorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious or jittery, feeling worried about what lies ahead.

parts.note: it sounds like a show-off cyclist, but a timepiece with a numeric display and no moving hands is meant

explanation.surface: A child boasts of riding a bike without holding on.
explanation.definitionFit: A timepiece showing numbers on a display has no hands, like this type of watch.

indicators.note: holding means the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: clever means skilful or adept

explanation.surface: Someone is dexterous while wielding an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy butcher's knife for hacking through meat and bone, a kind of chopper.

parts.note: matches in a knockout competition are played in rounds, so each is a game in a round

explanation.surface: A puzzle about games played with something circular.
explanation.definitionFit: Knockout football matches in a trophy competition are played round by round.

clue.text: Might it be served at a stag party?

definitions.text: Might it be served at a stag party?

parts.words: Might it be served at a stag party?
parts.note: a stag party is a groom's night out, but stag also suggests deer, and deer meat is the dish

explanation.surface: A question about the menu at a bachelor party.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is the British term for a groom's pre-wedding night out with friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer meat, a fitting dish for a party named after the male deer.

clue.text: Country or Empire with no politician

indicators.note: with no means the letters for a politician are taken away

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A choice between a nation or an empire lacking a statesman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish-language name for Ireland, an independent nation-state.

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters of page are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: An instruction to start writing on a new sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' looks like a verb about the book; it is the adjective, wide open.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide open, especially of a mouth gaping in wonder.

definitions.meaning: a small wading shorebird of the sandpiper family
a nautical measure, loosely a sea mile, used for speeds at sea

explanation.definitionFit: A sandpiper-like wader, and a nautical unit loosely used for a sea mile.

clue.text: Concluding passage is a bit of flamenco dancing

indicators.note: a bit of means only a portion of the words flamenco dancing is taken

explanation.surface: A closing section is part of a Spanish dance routine.
explanation.definitionFit: The final section of a piece of music, rounding it off.

clue.text: Second million that Dad's put into tinned food

indicators.note: put into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: pa is a word for dad; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A father has invested a second million into a canned-goods business.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand of canned luncheon meat, the classic tinned food.

definitions.meaning: read as de-crease: remove the creases from cloth
to settle disagreements, as you would smooth away differences

explanation.definitionFit: Pressing removes wrinkles from a garment, and the same phrasal verb means resolving disputes.

clue.text: Painting technique Pam is converted to

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pam has taken up a new style of painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link word but its letters go in the anagram; 'to' looks like a link but is added as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying on paint thickly so brush strokes stand proud of the canvas is this artistic method.

clue.text: Place of business for ruling class

definitions.meaning: the powerful group controlling society, the elite

explanation.definitionFit: A firm or shop is a business premises; the elite who hold power are also called by this name.
